title: Trapping and Blood-Sampling Small Mammals in Semi-Arid Environments
author: Pedro E. Cattan

steps.title: Prepare Personal Protective Equipment
steps.instruction: Wear appropriate protective gear based on the risk of infectious diseases.

substeps.instruction: If target or sympatric species are suspected to transmit infectious diseases, wear disposable gloves underneath and over thick gloves, a whole-body disposable suit (e.g. Tyvek™), and a filtered mask or respirator throughout the process.

steps.title: Survey Trapping Areas
steps.instruction: Visually inspect intended trapping areas for signs of micromammal presence.

substeps.instruction: Search for direct or indirect signs such as urine marks, droppings, hair, and burrows.

steps.title: Set and Mark Traps
steps.instruction: Deploy traps using thick gloves and a specific sampling strategy (e.g., transect, web design, or directed sampling).

substeps.instruction: Mark each trap with a unique code.
Set traps with chosen bait and bedding material.
Place devices on a horizontal, stable surface.
Locate traps in areas protected from extreme weather (e.g., under bushes, trees, or cactuses) or use shelter material.
Mark the site with a flag or flagging tape containing the trap code.
Georeference the trap location.

steps.title: Activate and Monitor Traps
steps.instruction: Keep traps open and baited during the target species' maximum activity period.

substeps.instruction: For nocturnal mammals: Activate from sunset until the next morning.
For diurnal mammals: Open immediately before foraging activity until the animals rest; monitor every 2-3 hours to prevent capture mortality due to thermal stress.

steps.title: Inspect Traps and Manage Captures
steps.instruction: Carefully inspect closed traps for captured animals.

substeps.instruction: Gently release non-target species (e.g., birds, reptiles) as soon as possible.
If animals exhibit 'trap-happy' behavior: Remove bait from empty traps and fold/place them in less accessible areas (e.g., over shrubs) to avoid inadvertent captures between grid activations.
If animals are reluctant to new objects: Close the trap with some bait inside at the same capture point.

steps.title: Transport Captured Animals
steps.instruction: Transport animals to an equipped laboratory while maintaining safety and environmental protection.

substeps.instruction: Wear protective clothing, goggles, a regular or filtered mask, and nitrile or latex gloves (use a respirator for suspected airborne infectious diseases).
Keep animals inside the trap wrapped in newspaper or thick plastic.
Place traps in a container (e.g., travel bag) to restrain them and protect them from extreme conditions while allowing air to enter.

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal inside the trap for immobilization and manipulation.

substeps.instruction: Use isoflurane for induction.
For manipulation, use isoflurane or an injectable agent such as ketamine/xylazine (KX) at 40-85/5-21 mg/Kg.
Use warming (heating) pads to prevent hypothermia and improve peripheral blood flow, checking temperature regularly to avoid overheating.

steps.title: Prepare for Blood Withdrawal
steps.instruction: Verify animal weight and prepare the venipuncture site.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the animal; only sample individuals weighing more than 20 g (maximum extraction is 1% of body weight).
Shave areas with hair cover to facilitate withdrawal.
Disinfect the clipped venipuncture area with ethanol.

steps.title: Perform Blood Withdrawal
steps.instruction: Extract a minimum of 0.2 ml of peripheral venous blood using the site and needle size specific to the species.

substeps.instruction: Octodon sp., Rattus sp., and Abrocoma bennetti: Saphenous vein using 19 or 21G needles.
Phyllotis darwini and Mus musculus: Submandibular zone (union of orbital and submandibular vein) with a 21G needle. For P. darwini under KX, saphenous vein using 23 or 21G needles.
Mus musculus (alternative): Jugular extraction with a 1 ml 25G syringe (perform very slowly).
Thylamys elegans, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus, and Abrothrix sp.: Jugular vein with a 1 ml 25G syringe (perform very slowly). For Abrothrix sp. under KX, saphenous vein using 23 or 21G needles.
Lagomorphs (Oryctolagus cuniculus, Lepus europaeus): Ear vein with a 1 ml 25G syringe, or saphenous vein with a 3 ml 21 or 23G syringe.

steps.title: Manage Fluid Volume
steps.instruction: Replace extracted blood volume with physiological serum (saline) subcutaneously.

substeps.instruction: Administer 0.2 ml before blood withdrawal using a 1 ml 25G syringe.
If more blood is obtained, replace the difference in volume with saline afterwards.

steps.title: Process Blood Samples
steps.instruction: Store blood samples based on the intended analysis.

substeps.instruction: For DNA preservation: Place blood in cryovials or microcentrifuge tubes and immediately mix in a 1:1 proportion with 6 M Guanidine-HCl 0.2 M EDTA; store at room temperature.

For serological techniques: Do not mix with Guanidine-HCl; allow blood to coagulate in the tube, retrieve serum via microcentrifuge, and freeze if not used immediately. The clot can also be frozen for later molecular techniques.

steps.title: Mark Individuals
steps.instruction: Apply unique identifiers to prevent resampling.

substeps.instruction: Mark both ears with a uniquely coded metallic ear tag.
Alternatively, use hair clipping, one ear tag per individual, or an identification chip.

steps.title: Recover and Release Animals
steps.instruction: Ensure animals are fully recovered from anesthesia before release.

substeps.instruction: Wait for complete recovery (approximately 1 minute for isoflurane; 30-60 minutes for KX depending on species).
Transport the animal back to the exact point of capture using the transport method described previously and release.
